note: Bci only: Banco de Chile's card pages answered with a captcha and its 'tarifas claras' page didn't answer, Santander Chile's site refused the request (403), and BancoEstado's returned no tariff, so Bci, among the largest card issuers, is the one bank whose full range could be read. Bci's tariff of charges for individuals (updated 7 May 2025, read again 30 October 2026) and its table of card interest (updated 15 November 2025), read in full: every personal Visa and Mastercard it prices (31; the Empresario and Business cards aren't written). Each card's yearly administration charge comes in two parts: a half-yearly charge in UF, waived in full when the card's purchases in Chile average more than a stated UF figure a month over the six months (10 UF on most cards, 13 on BciPlus Classic, Gold and Platinum, 40 on the AAdvantage cards and BciPlus Signature, Black and Infinite), written as spending six times that figure over the half year (the 50% discount on a lower average is a step not written, nor the waiver for holders of a Bci current-account plan, which the game doesn't check); and a monthly charge in UF for the cards the tariff names (cards it doesn't name pay between UF 0.06 and 0.10 a month, a range not written). The monthly charge isn't made in a month the card isn't used and carries no debt, which the game doesn't distinguish. Charges are made in pesos at the UF's value on the first of the month; at the Unidad de Fomento's value on 1 October 2026, 41,065.38 pesos (the tax service's table), each is written in whole pesos. A purchase abroad costs 2.5% of its amount, except on the cards the tariff exempts. A cash advance in Chile costs nothing. Interest is 9.84% to 48.96% a year on every card (the table names the Visa and Mastercard ranges together), written at the top with the bottom as the range's lowest. No minimum payment, grace period or late fee is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added two banks. CMR Falabella (Promotora CMR Falabella S.A., Banco Falabella's card issuer, the country's largest card issuer by cards in use) was chosen as the next large issuer that publishes its terms: its information on interest, commissions, charges, collection costs and taxes on the CMR Falabella cards (in force from 15 October 2026), read in full. Its revolving purchases are priced by the card's limit, at a maximum effective 3.41% a month on limits up to 2,058,137 pesos, 2.83% up to 8,232,546 and 2.49% above, written as 3.41% a month with 2.49% as the range's lowest; cash advances are priced on the same tiers. Its monthly administration commission, VAT included, is written for contracts signed now (the figure with no date limit in each column): 0.085 UF on the CMR, CMR Visa and CMR Mastercard, 0.22 UF on the Platinum cards, 0.35 UF on the CMR Visa Signature and CMR Mastercard Elite, and 0.135 UF on the CMR Mastercard Contactless, each in whole pesos at the UF's value on 1 October 2026 (41,065.38 pesos); the CMR Visa Contactless and CMR PRO, whose only figure is for contracts signed until 5 October 2023, aren't written; the discount on spending 6,600,000 or 18,000,000 pesos in a calendar year, which runs from the next month to the end of the next year, isn't written. The late interest, at most 3.41% a month, is written as the penalty rate; the collection costs (9%, 6% and 3% of the overdue debt in UF bands, after twenty days) and the stamp tax (at a rate the sheet doesn't give) aren't written. No minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee is stated. Scotiabank Chile was chosen as one of the country's largest banks: its table of credit card interest and maintenance commissions (dated 14 October 2026), read in full, gives every card type the same interest, 10.05% to 41.02% a year, written at the top with the bottom as the range's lowest, and each card's maintenance commission as a yearly peso range from nothing (with a product plan, which the game doesn't check) to a maximum, written at the maximum; the Business, Business Pyme and Corporate cards aren't written. Its tariff of cards issued from 15 November 2025 (a table read by eye: its figures are an image) gives the purchases abroad charge, 2.50% on the Gold and Platinum and 0.00% on the Black, Signature, Singular Infinite and Wealth, written as the foreign transaction fee (the Singular, Infinite, Platinum Plus, Internacional, Nacional and Universal carry none there, so none is written); its cash advance abroad (2.50% plus 2.50 US dollars) isn't written, nor the plan discounts. No minimum payment, grace period or late charge is stated. Tried and not used: Itaú Chile's site sits behind Incapsula and BICE's refused the request behind a captcha (403); Banco Ripley's home page answered but wasn't searched for a tariff in this pass.
